The in-app water tier is open across the entire Bolt footprint, for now.

close.title: From the Aegean to the Gulf, in one app.
close.body: Bolt owns the demand across Europe's and the Gulf's most water-bound markets. Navier supplies the one surface no ride-hail player has claimed. Start with the Greek islands, or commit to the network.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the marinas and piers already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 sold out), decarbonization mandates turned diesel fleets into liabilities, and the hybrid removed the range excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

objections.concern: Ground ride-hail is our core — why move onto water?
objections.response: Water is the one urban surface Bolt's mission of cheaper, cleaner, car-free mobility hasn't reached. Across the Saronic, the Dalmatian coast and the Gulf, the sea is the fastest line between two points — and no super-app owns it yet.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for the Mediterranean and Gulf?
objections.response: Most coastal and island hops are short — inside the all-electric Pioneer II's 70 nm envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer island and cross-gulf legs up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: We operate in 45+ countries — how do we launch without huge overhead?
objections.response: You don't build or run the fleet. Navier brings vessels, captains and maintenance; Bolt brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand. Each coastal city is a self-contained pilot on existing berths — no new infrastructure.

objections.concern: Will a water tier fit Bolt's value positioning?
objections.response: Foiling's low energy per passenger-mile is exactly what makes an affordable water option viable. It's cleaner and car-free — on-brand for Bolt — and the resort corridors fund the launch while commuters get a faster crossing.

markets.why_navier_now: Every Dalmatian leg (Split–Trogir 8nm, Split–Brač 12nm, Dubrovnik–Kotor 40nm) is inside Pioneer II range — no long-range hull needed for the core network.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel ferry/excursion boat: faster, on-demand, quiet and all-electric in protected Adriatic waters. Against the coast road: a direct island line that skips the summer jam.

markets.why_now: Egypt is targeting 30M tourists, with the Red Sea its fastest-growing coast and a new wave of resort and marina development at El Gouna, Sahl Hasheesh and the Red Sea Riviera. markets.why_navier_now: Every core Red Sea and Cairo corridor is ≤16nm — squarely Pioneer II, commercial today. The piers exist: El Gouna's lagoon network, Hurghada Marina, Sharm's jetties, and the Cairo corniche. No regional Quanta-LR leg is needed to start.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel excursion boat: faster to the reefs, no fumes over protected coral, and bookable on demand. Against the Cairo road: a flying river crossing that sidesteps the bridges entirely.

objections.concern: Nile permitting is complex.

hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Dublin Bay — Docklands to Dún Laoghaire and Howth, plus the Dalkey and Howth island leisure hops — booked in the Bolt app.

markets.why_now: Dublin's coastal suburbs are commuter-dense and the bay is underused for transport. Howth and Dalkey are major day-trip destinations. The DART and coast roads jam at peak. Pioneer II is commercial now and every Dublin Bay leg sits inside its range.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the Docklands pier, a foiling hop down the bay to Dún Laoghaire or out to Howth, a Bolt bike on arrival. The bay becomes a fast spine alongside the DART.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is an established ridehail brand in Dublin. A water tier adds a premium, scenic, all-electric layer on the bay corridors where peak road and rail congestion is worst — no vessels on Bolt's books.
markets.why_navier_now: Every Dublin Bay leg (Docklands–Dún Laoghaire 6.5nm, Docklands–Howth 7nm) is comfortably inside Pioneer II range. The Dublin–Holyhead crossing (67nm) sits at the edge of Pioneer's envelope and is staged as a roadmap corridor, rendered honestly rather than promised as a day-one service.
markets.differentiation: Against the DART/road at peak: a direct, scenic water line with zero local emissions. Against a charter boat: on-demand, in-app and electric rather than booked and diesel.

markets.label: Italy — Amalfi, Capri & Venice
markets.summary: Italy concentrates three of the world's most iconic water markets — Venice's lagoon, the Amalfi/Capri coast, and the Ligurian Portofino riviera. All are dense, premium, and served today by crowded diesel vaporetti and excursion boats. Bolt's Italian ridehail brand is the front door to a co-branded foiling tier.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Venice, Amalfi & the Riviera
hero.subtitle: Foil the lagoon and the Amalfi coast at speed, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Venice's lagoon, the Amalfi/Capri coast and the Portofino riviera — booked in the Bolt app.

markets.why_now: Italy draws ~60M visitors a year, with Venice, Amalfi and the Ligurian riviera among the most water-dependent destinations on earth. The vaporetti and excursion boats are slow, crowded and diesel. Venice has active anti-wake and decarbonization pressure that favours foiling. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every leg.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the waterfront, a foiling hop across the lagoon or along the Amalfi coast, seamless return — a premium chain on the corridors where the diesel boat is slowest.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is an established ridehail brand in Italy. A water tier extends that brand onto the country's signature waterways, aligned with Venice's wake and emissions agenda — without Bolt operating vessels.
markets.why_navier_now: Every Italian leg here is short (Venice–Lido 1.5nm, Positano–Amalfi 4nm, Sorrento–Capri 9.5nm), squarely in Pioneer II's commercial envelope. Low-wake foiling is a particularly strong fit for Venice's fragile lagoon.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel vaporetto/excursion boat: faster, quiet, low-wake and all-electric — exactly what Venice's anti-wake rules reward. Against the road on the Amalfi coast: there barely is one; the water is the fast path.

markets.label: Nigeria — Lagos (Lagos Lagoon)
markets.summary: Lagos is arguably the single largest urban water-commuter opportunity on earth — a ~20M+ megacity built around a lagoon, where short crow-flies trips take 2–3 hours across chronically gridlocked bridges. The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA) already regulates a growing terminal network, but the lagoon carries a tiny fraction of trips on aging diesel boats. Bolt holds the largest ride-hail market share in Nigeria — a co-branded foiling lagoon-transit tier is a textbook congestion-beating overlay across the islands.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Lagos Lagoon
hero.subtitle: Foil across the lagoon — CMS to Victoria Island, Lekki and Ikorodu — booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling lagoon-transit tier that bypasses the bridges, anchored on the dense island CBD core and scaling onto the mass Ikorodu commuter corridor.

markets.why_now: Lagos State has made water transport a strategic priority for a decade and already has the regulator (LASWA) and terminals in place — the missing piece is a clean, fast, safe, reliable platform. Bolt has the largest market share in Nigeria and the riders already in-app. Pioneer II clears the entire core lagoon network today; the zero-wake stable foiling ride is itself the safety-and-trust story the lagoon needs.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the CMS or Falomo terminal, a foiling hop across the lagoon to VI, Lekki or Ikorodu, a Bolt ride on arrival — the bridge-bypass folded into the daily commute.
markets.partner_context: Bolt holds the largest ride-hail market share in Nigeria (reported >60%), with Lagos its dominant city. An in-app lagoon-transit tier across the islands is a congestion-beating revenue layer in Bolt's single strongest African market.
markets.why_navier_now: The entire core lagoon network is in Pioneer II range today: CMS–Victoria Island (~1.5–4nm), Ikoyi–CMS (~2.5nm), CMS–Apapa (~4nm), and the mass-commuter flagship CMS–Ikorodu (~13nm). The longer growth corridors (Epe Free Zone ~30nm, Badagry ~28nm) are honestly staged on Quanta-LR.
markets.differentiation: Against the 2–3-hour bridge gridlock and the aging diesel ferry: a fast, clean, software-monitored, zero-wake platform whose stability and safety are the value proposition — the missing trust layer LASWA's network needs.

proof_points.claim: Lagos is the largest urban water-commuter opportunity on earth.
proof_points.evidence: A ~20–25M megacity built around a lagoon where road trips of a few km take 2–3 hours across a handful of jammed bridges.

proof_points.claim: The regulator and terminals already exist.
proof_points.evidence: LASWA regulates and is expanding terminals (CMS, Falomo, Ikorodu, Apapa, Badagry); a ready-made regulatory backbone.

proof_points.claim: The core lagoon network is inside Pioneer II range.
proof_points.evidence: CMS–VI ~1.5–4nm, CMS–Apapa ~4nm, CMS–Ikorodu ~13nm.

proof_points.claim: Bolt is Nigeria's largest ride-hail brand.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt holds the largest market share in Nigeria (reported >60%), with Lagos its dominant city.

objections.concern: Is mass-commuter affordability viable?
objections.response: We run a tiered model: a high-WTP Victoria Island / Lekki corporate tier cross-subsidizes the mass Ikorodu commuter corridor — sustainable rollout economics in partnership with the state operator.

objections.concern: Lagoon debris and safety are real risks.
objections.response: Exactly the gap: a stable, software-monitored, zero-wake foiling platform with rigorous training is safer and more reliable than the diesel incumbent — safety is the proposition, not a caveat.

objections.concern: Is the demand really there beyond pilots?
objections.response: The Ikorodu–CMS corridor is already the busiest existing ferry line; we anchor on proven flows and the high-WTP island CBD, not speculative routes.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a Lagos lagoon-transit tier with Bolt — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor on the island CBD core (CMS–VI–Ikoyi–Apapa), scaling onto the mass Ikorodu commuter corridor.
markets.close: Lagos wants to move onto the water, already has the regulator, and Bolt already has the riders — a Bolt-branded foiling tier is the clean, safe, fast platform that finally bypasses the bridges.
markets.end_state: A Lagos Lagoon network — island CBD core plus the Ikorodu mass-commuter corridor — with a Quanta-LR growth-corridor roadmap, all booked in the Bolt app.

markets.summary: Spain is Europe's #1 leisure-boating and second-busiest tourism market, with the densest island-and-coast water demand in the western Med — the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — almost none of it earning revenue in-app. Bolt already runs ride-hail across Spanish cities; the water tier is the missing leg between the airport pier and the island.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Spain, the western-Med island shuttle
hero.subtitle: Turn the Balearic and Costa crossings into a flying, in-app water tier.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded foiling water tier across the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — booked in the same app as the car, all-electric, no wake, no diesel-ferry timetable.

markets.why_now: Spain hosts ~85M visitors a year and the Balearics alone draw ~16M; the islands are choking on diesel ferries and rental cars while Formentera, Mallorca and Ibiza tighten anchoring and emissions rules. A clean, quiet, on-demand foiling hop is exactly what the regulators and the resorts are asking for — and no super-app has the water leg.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt car to the pier, a foiling Pioneer II across the water, a Bolt scooter on the island. The water leg books door-to-door, captain-partners instead of driver-partners.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is the largest European-owned mobility platform, already operating ride-hail and micromobility across Spain. Spain is a top-five Bolt market by trips and the natural place to prove a Med water tier before extending east.
markets.why_navier_now: Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the short Balearic and Costa hops on a single charge; the Palma–Ibiza–Menorca regional legs (75–130nm) come into reach with Quanta-LR on the 2026+ roadmap. Spain's berths already exist — Palma, Ibiza Town, Formentera (La Savina), Puerto Banús — so we need a pedestal, not a port.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel fast-ferry: half the door-to-door time, zero wake into protected Posidonia seagrass zones, no fixed timetable, and a fare booked in an app riders already have. Against a private RIB charter: a fraction of the cost and fully electric.

proof_points.claim: The Balearics are a top global leisure-marine market.
proof_points.evidence: Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca and Formentera draw ~16M visitors a year with intense inter-island and coast-to-island water demand.

proof_points.claim: The corridors are protected and emissions-sensitive.
proof_points.evidence: Formentera caps daily vehicles and the Balearic Posidonia decree restricts anchoring and wake — favouring a quiet, electric, foiling hull.

proof_points.claim: The berths already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Palma, Ibiza Town, La Savina (Formentera), Port de Sóller, Puerto Banús and Marbella are working harbours — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

proof_points.claim: Bolt already owns the rider in Spain.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt operates ride-hail and micromobility across Spanish cities; the water leg slots into an app riders already carry.

objections.concern: The Balearic crossings (Palma–Ibiza) are too long for an 8-pax foiler.

objections.concern: Ferries already run these routes.

objections.concern: Seasonality — Spain's water demand is summer-heavy.
objections.response: True, and the model sizes the Prove fleet to the shoulder-season floor; summer is upside. The same hulls redeploy across the Med as the network grows.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a Spain water tier with Bolt, starting with a 2-boat Prove fleet on the Costa del Sol / Costa Brava capillary hops in 2026 H2, scaling across the Balearic islands as berth agreements land.
markets.close: Spain is the densest leisure-water market in Europe and Bolt already owns the rider. The water tier is the one leg no one has flown — let's fly it.

markets.label: Thailand — Phuket & Phang Nga (Andaman)
markets.summary: Phuket and Phang Nga form the highest-density resort-and-island cluster in Southeast Asia, with a huge tourist island-hopping market today served by diesel speedboats and longtails. From the Phuket east-coast marinas, Phang Nga Bay's limestone karsts, Koh Yao, Phi Phi and Krabi all sit inside Pioneer II range, and the Andaman is calendar-predictable by monsoon half-year. Bolt is the leading challenger ride-hail brand in Thailand and is live in Phuket — a co-branded foiling tier turns the island-hop into a fast, clean, in-app service.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Phuket & the Andaman
hero.subtitle: Foil from the Phuket marinas out to Phang Nga, Phi Phi and Krabi, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling island-hopping tier across the Andaman's densest resort cluster, anchored on the Phuket east-coast marina spine.

markets.why_now: Phuket is one of the world's busiest island-tourism markets, and its day-trip and resort-transfer volume runs on aging diesel speedboats. Bolt is live in Phuket and is the main challenger to Grab in Thailand, so the app and the riders are already here. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the entire core Andaman cluster; the monsoon calendar is predictable, and Phang Nga Bay is shielded year-round.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car from Phuket airport to the marina, a foiling hop to Koh Yao or Phi Phi, a Bolt ride on arrival — the island-hop folded into the trip people already book.
markets.partner_context: Bolt has operated in Thailand since 2020 and is live in Phuket, Bangkok, Chiang Mai and beyond — the leading challenger to Grab. Phuket's tourist island-hopping demand is a textbook in-app water tier in a market where Bolt already has riders and brand.
markets.why_navier_now: The core Andaman cluster is Pioneer II routine today: Phang Nga Bay (~12nm), Koh Yao Noi (~12nm), Phi Phi (~25nm), Krabi/Ao Nang (~30nm), even Similan (~50nm). The longer cross-coast and cross-border legs (Koh Samui ~190nm, Langkawi ~110nm) are honestly staged on Quanta-LR, never faked on a 70nm boat.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel speedboat and longtail: a quiet, stable, zero-wake foiling ride that is faster, cleaner and dramatically safer — in a market with real day-trip safety memory — all bookable in the Bolt app.

proof_points.claim: Phuket/Phang Nga is the densest resort-and-island cluster in SEA.
proof_points.evidence: Aman, Six Senses, Banyan Tree, Soneva, Anantara and dozens more anchor a huge day-trip island-hopping market.

proof_points.claim: The core Andaman cluster is inside Pioneer II range.

proof_points.claim: Bolt is live in Phuket.

proof_points.claim: Phang Nga Bay is a year-round operating window.
proof_points.evidence: The Phuket landmass shields Phang Nga Bay from the SW monsoon — calendar-predictable year-round operability.

objections.concern: Isn't this a luxury-charter play, not a Bolt play?
objections.response: The hospitality density is the backdrop; the Bolt gap is the high-volume tourist island-hop — airport-to-marina-to-island in the app riders already use.

objections.concern: The SW monsoon degrades open crossings.
objections.response: True for exposed legs May–Oct — but Phang Nga Bay is shielded year-round and the calendar is predictable, so we right-size seasonally rather than pretend it away.

objections.concern: Candela is already in Thailand.
objections.response: On short routes we compete head-to-head; our gap is the Andaman cluster density plus the Quanta-LR cross-coast and cross-border reach (Samui, Langkawi) where the gap is widest.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand an Andaman island-hopping water tier with Bolt — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor on the Phuket east-coast marinas, scaling across Phang Nga, Phi Phi and Krabi.
markets.close: Phuket is one of the world's great island-tourism markets, and Bolt already has the riders — a Bolt-branded foiling tier turns the diesel island-hop into a fast, clean, in-app signature ride.
markets.end_state: A Phuket–Phang Nga island-hopping network with Pioneer II across the core cluster and a Quanta-LR cross-coast/cross-border roadmap, all booked in the Bolt app.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — UAE, the anchor market
hero.subtitle: Foil between Dubai's jetties and on to Abu Dhabi, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Dubai's jetty network, scaling to a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor — the flagship of the Bolt water network.

markets.why_now: Dubai has the world's densest cluster of luxury hotel and residence jetties, a government actively promoting marine transport, and a clientele that already pays for premium transfers. The Dubai–Abu Dhabi road is a 90-minute-plus drive the water can shortcut. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every intra-Dubai jetty hop.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app and wallet: a Bolt car to the jetty, a foiling hop between Palm resorts or across to Abu Dhabi, seamless return — a single premium chain on the corridors where road congestion and heat make driving least attractive.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is expanding its regional premium ambitions. The UAE is where a co-branded marine tier has the highest willingness-to-pay and the strongest government tailwind — the natural anchor to prove the model before replicating it across the network.
markets.why_navier_now: Every intra-Dubai jetty leg (0.5–1.2nm) is trivially inside Pioneer II range. The Dubai Marina–Abu Dhabi Corniche corridor (55.8nm) sits inside the 70nm Pioneer envelope — a genuine near-term regional run, not a roadmap aspiration.
markets.differentiation: Against the chauffeur car: comparable cost, far faster jetty-to-jetty, air-conditioned cabin and a skyline view with zero local emissions. Against the diesel water taxi: foiling-quiet, on-demand and in-app.

proof_points.claim: Dubai has the densest luxury-jetty network in the world.

proof_points.evidence: Dubai's marine-transport agenda and abundant licensed marina infrastructure support a water tier.

markets.close: The UAE is the highest-value, highest-readiness water-mobility market on earth — the natural anchor to prove Bolt-on-water before the network replicates it.
markets.end_state: A dense Dubai jetty network plus a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor, the flagship of the Bolt water network.
